review_notes: Kailali police report confirms the 13-year-old boy trapped by the July 13 landslide died in hospital the next day; one fatality.
At Kyāng in Modi-4, the occupants had left the stuck jeep before it was buried; Parbat police explicitly reported no human casualties.
July 24 landslide destroyed and blocked the Ramche–Maneshwora road at Karkalebari, cutting off vehicle access to nearby villages.
The Tuin Khola landslide obstructed the Narayanghat–Muglin highway; traffic resumed after the debris was cleared.
Nagarik describes landslide-related road blockages at named Surkhet locations, including Lade and Pokhare; this classification is a road obstruction. The article mentions multiple sites.
A July 5 landslide in Nuwakot Tol, Purbi Chauki-4, killed one six-month-old infant; the mother was injured. Separate Bajhang relief discussion is unrelated.
Police report that the July 17 landslide at Shirbari buried and killed pedestrian Deu Prasad Gharti; the separate Kholabang road blockage is not this fatality.
An August 4 slide at Bangabagar, Dilashaini-6, completely blocked the Mahakali Highway from 7 a.m.; historical damage from earlier years is only context.
A large rock-bearing landslide fell from above onto the Waling–Jagat road at Lasune and buried the carriageway. The account supports a mixed landslide rather than isolated rockfall.
Rain-triggered slide from above at Bhalupahad, Phedikhola-2, completely obstructed the Siddhartha Highway from about 6:30 a.m.
A dry slide near Lumsera, Tila-3, buried the Jumla stretch of the Karnali Highway and stopped both long- and short-distance traffic.
During road widening in Marsyangdi-2, a rock-bearing slide buried excavator driver Vikki Mahato; doctors declared him dead at the hospital.
A September 5 dry slide near Tamail bazaar blocked the Jayaprithvi Highway; vehicles and passengers were stranded.
Although the report also discusses flood warnings, it documents an actual 10:15 p.m. slide at Nibu, Melamchi-2, that blocked the Bhotechour–Kaule road.
A dry slide at Khopang, Gosaikunda-5, completely blocked the Pasang Lhamu Highway, stranding buses, ambulances and freight vehicles.
A slide near Jawangkhola, Benighat Rorang, blocked Prithvi Highway on July 16; traffic resumed after clearance the following morning.
Police identified three deaths after a rock-bearing slide near Siddhababa crushed a truck and car: the truck driver and two car passengers.

The September 28 follow-up for the September 22 Kerauja trekking-trail slide reports four deaths and six injured; the claimed six confuses casualties and deaths. An initial report has inconsistent preliminary totals.
The report calls the rain-triggered event near Siddhababa a mudslide that deposited debris across and obstructed Siddhartha Highway, supporting debris-flow-type road obstruction.
A woman collecting house-plastering soil in Lamahi-6 was buried when a mound collapsed during digging; the described excavation-bank collapse is not a natural landslide.
A landslide at Hakpara, Hariharpurgadhi, blocked Madan Bhandari Highway; the separate BP Highway obstruction was flooding in Kavre, not another Sindhuli landslide.

Multiple reports describe a debris/mud-laden flow at Tilgaun and explicitly confirm no human casualties, so the existing claimed deaths=0 is correct. The requested correct_deaths action is an audit/queue false positive; do not replace supported zero with an unsupported value. Remove that action before strict validation. [Normalization: the blank claimed death value means not_reported; explicit source confirmation of no human casualties is encoded as final_deaths=0.]
The June 12 slope failure near Syaulibazaar, Rampur-1, blocked the Kaligandaki Corridor road until the debris was removed on June 13.
The dry slide at Ranka, Tatopani-1, blocked the Jumla section of Karnali Highway for several hours; the report separately confirms zero casualties.
Officials reported no loss of human life from ongoing Manang flooding and slides, including the June 16 Ngawal landslide that dammed the Marsyangdi River.
